newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU can live with more intvn grain - Bonn official.
newsitem.headline: EU can live with more intvn grain - Bonn official.

text.p: The European Union would be able to live with a rise in grain intervention stocks in 1997 after it depleted its public stocks in earlier seasons, Franz-Josef Feiter, state secretary in the Bonn farm ministry said.
"We don't fear new surpluses, after all stores were nearly completely empty," he said in response to questions at a news conference during Germany's "Green Week" farm fair.
"We're quite relaxed about the whole issue."
But he said the ministry was thinking about suggesting a possible rise in the set-aside area for the 1998 harvest after the 1997 set-aside rate was halved to five percent.
Feiter had stepped in for farm minister Jochen Borchert, who could not attend the press conference because of urgent parliamentary business in Bonn.
Commission officials believe EU grain intervention stocks could rise to more than 10 million tonnes at the end of the 1996-97 (July-June) season from 2.8 million at the end of 1995-96.
Other forecasts see 15 or even 20 million tonnes building up if the EU cannot export surplus grain to the world market.
Volumes would rise further in 1997-98 after another huge EU crop this year, on the cards due to an expanded area and given favourable weather.
Critics say this could reverse the success of farm reform and would annoy tax-payers especially in Germany, where the bulk of EU intervention grain is kept.
